ownership: source-only preparation; root owns runtime, peer review, integration, and closure
root_cause: JsonTree concatenates object keys with dots, and Network and Framework split the resulting string on dots. Literal dotted keys and nested paths therefore become indistinguishable.

changes: Shared JSON key-path codec quotes keys containing dot, brackets, or backslash as JSON string bracket segments; ordinary dotted paths retain their previous meaning.
JsonTree emits the distinct path strings; Network resolves them through the shared parser.
Framework parses in the extension realm before chrome.scripting injection, then traverses the exact segments in the page realm. The persisted config remains the single key_path string.

compatibility_limit: The single-string bracket grammar cannot distinguish an old legacy recipe whose literal key text already equals a syntactically valid bracket path, such as ["feeds.news"]. Ordinary legacy dotted strings, including feeds.news, retain nested traversal. Zero-collision historical compatibility would require persisted syntax metadata; root must decide whether this exotic collision warrants it before integration.
